title: Mapping the European Rights Retention Community of Practice: Mobilising Change
content:
Blog post by Clara Riera

Rights retention is gaining momentum across Europe. To make this progress more visible, we mapped where members of the European Rights Retention Community of Practice are based and where interest in it is growing.

Since KR21 project partner SPARC Europe launched this community in late 2024, it has grown to almost 725 members worldwide, with over 665 from 31 European countries. Its 11th meeting on 8 October 2026 marked almost two years of regular exchange among researchers, librarians, policy professionals and others working to advance rights retention. 

This new map is a simple way to visualise this growing community. It shows where members are joining from, highlighting the spread of interest across Europe and, more broadly, the community’s international reach. The map reflects one of the community’s main aims: supporting the development of rights retention in institutional policymaking as a route to achieving 100% open access in Europe.

title: Innovation Act, Industrial Access Charter, ERA Act: Who Will Fix Copyright for Research Partnerships?
content:
Right from the start of the current mandate of the European Commission, there has been an emphasis on promoting innovation. Seen as essential for ensuring competitiveness and resilience in an increasingly uncertain world, this has been a constant theme across legislation, policy and funding.

In this context, we have seen a drive to address Europe’s ‘Innovation Paradox’ – the fact that the bloc has a very strong research sector, but that this does not translate into new products, services, companies and markets. There have been important steps to address this by building stronger bridges between research and innovation, starting already in mid-2024 with the decision to combine the policy briefs on research and innovation under one Commissioner – Ekaterina Zaharieva.

2026 nonetheless looks set to be the year when things get a lot more concrete. Since last month, we have had a draft of a European Innovation Act. There has also been the new Charter on Industrial Access to Research and Technology Infrastructures. The planned European Research Area Act later this year, and copyright reforms next, both offer further opportunities.
